witness_evidence: Analysis from emulator survey: no 64-bit x86 engine has a wasm JIT backend. blink JIT relies on runtime native codegen (copying compiled C micro-ops) which is impossible in sandboxed wasm => interpreter mode ~10x slower per blink README -j note. Box64 has no wasm dynarec at all. QEMU TCG-to-wasm is interpreter-grade. A VST processing a 128-sample block at 48kHz must finish in ~2.7ms; under a wasm interpreter doing full x86-64 emulation of Wine+plugin DSP, per-block cost is very likely 10-100x over budget for non-trivial synths. Realtime live audio is at-risk; OFFLINE/non-realtime rendering (process faster-than-or-slower-than realtime into a buffer) is the achievable mode. This must be reflected in the ADR and the product scope.
